definitions.explanation: A time far in the past. Used to refer to events, periods, or memories from a long time ago.

examples.japanese: それは{遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}の{話|はなし}だ。
examples.english: That's a story from long ago.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}、この{辺|あた}りは{海|うみ}だったそうだ。
examples.english: I hear that long ago, this area was the sea.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}のことなんて{遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}のことで、もうほとんど{覚|おぼ}えていない。
examples.english: Things from my childhood feel like the distant past — I can barely remember them anymore.

notes:
A phrase combining {遠|とお}い (distant/far) and {昔|むかし} (the past/old times). Functions as a set expression to emphasize how far back in time something was. Often used to begin stories or reminiscences, similar to English "long, long ago."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}の{話|はなし} — a story from long ago
- {遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}のこと — something from the distant past
- {遠|とお}い{昔|むかし}に — long ago (adverbial use)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大昔|おおむかし} — a very long time ago (single compound word; can feel even more distant)
- {昔々|むかしむかし} — once upon a time (fairy-tale opening; more formulaic)
- ずっと{前|まえ} — a long time ago (more casual, everyday expression)
- {古|いにしえ} — antiquity; ancient times (literary/poetic register)
